# Jubilees Chapter 43 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob hears Joseph lives; the descent to Egypt; Jacob before Pharaoh

---

**43:1** When Jacob heard that Joseph was alive and that he was ruler over all Egypt, his spirit was greatly moved. He said: "It is enough; my son Joseph is still alive. I will go and see him before I die."

**43:2** Jacob arose with his sons and traveled to Egypt. They came to Goshen, and Joseph went up to meet his father Jacob.

**43:3** Joseph fell on his father's neck and wept greatly. Jacob said: "Now I am content to die, since I have seen your face — that you are still alive."

**43:4** Joseph brought his father and his brothers and presented them before Pharaoh, and they bowed down before him.

**43:5** Pharaoh said to Jacob: "How old are you?" Jacob said: "The years of my sojourning are one hundred and thirty years. Few and difficult have been the years of my life, and they have not attained to the years of my fathers during their sojourning."

**43:6** Pharaoh blessed Jacob and all his sons, and Jacob and his sons ate bread before Pharaoh.

**43:7** Joseph gave his father and his brothers a possession in Egypt in the land of Goshen — the best of the land. He provided them with food. And Jacob and his sons settled in Egypt, in the land of Goshen.

**43:8** The famine continued throughout all the land of Egypt and all the land of Canaan. Joseph gathered all the silver of the Egyptians and of the Canaanites in exchange for the grain they bought.

**43:9** All the Egyptians came to Joseph saying: "Give us food, for our silver is exhausted." Joseph said: "Give your livestock, and I will give you food in exchange for your livestock."

**43:10** They brought their livestock to Joseph — horses, donkeys, oxen, sheep, and goats — and Joseph gave them food in exchange. That year he received all their livestock.

**43:11** When the next year came, they came again and said: "We have nothing left but our bodies and our land. Buy us and our land for food, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh."

**43:12** Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, except for the land of the priests, because the priests received an allotment from Pharaoh. And Joseph made it a statute for all the land of Egypt to this day.

---

*LOGOS notes: Jacob's speech before Pharaoh (v.5) is one of the most moving passages in the patriarchal narratives. "Few and difficult" renders the Ge'ez more precisely than the traditional "evil" (though "evil" is also a valid rendering of the underlying term). The famine management narrative (vv.8-12) demonstrates Joseph's economic genius and explains the basis for Egyptian serfdom.*
